label: late-position / delimiter in long sequences, gated by first token (t,d,k,r,...) and current token (b,z,0,n,e,q,g,f,<DEL>)
explanation: Never fires in the copy phase (0 of ~546k copy steps on dev). About half the mass is at the <DEL> step and half on the last few original tokens. It is strongly concentrated at late absolute positions (t = 7-9, about 90% of mass) and therefore in long sequences (L = 9 holds 66% of mass, L = 8 holds 28%; nearly silent for L <= 6). Within that window, firing depends on content. (1) The first original token, which is also what gets output at <DEL>: t, d, k, r, 3, 2 and p have 2-4x lift. (2) The current input token: <DEL>, b, z, 0, n, e, q, g, f, with b the strongest (3.8x); w, u and h are nearly never active. It also favours first occurrences (in_first, 91% of mass) and sequences with more digits. The top activations are b/z/e at position 7-8 followed by <DEL>, in sequences starting with d/t/k/p. Position alone (t >= 7, phase <= 1) catches about 90% of the mass at only 11% precision. Adding the first-token and current-token sets gives dev P 0.53 / R 0.51 / mass 0.64. The remaining variance looks like a distributed content code that a simple predicate does not capture.
